subject: Unexpected latency jitter impacting Checkoutly checkout API
messages:
From: Ali Khatri <ali@checkoutly.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@checkoutly.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden jitter on /v1/generate - Checkout failing (high p99)

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a sharp jump in p99 latency for our checkout flows hitting Redwood's gen endpoint around 07:50 PDT. CPU across our app tier looks fine; errors are low but the user-visible checkout takes 3-4x longer and a few sessions have timed out. This is impacting revenue; we had to toggle to a reduced QPS window while we triage.

Attached is a short p99 report and a small sample of traces we captured (runtime-sample-logs-15jun.zip). Can you confirm this is on your side and what the expected next steps are?

I can be on a call in 15 if needed.

- Ali
Senior SRE, Checkoutly

[attachment: p99-scaling-report-20270615.pdf]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ali Khatri <ali@checkoutly.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden jitter on /v1/generate - Checkout failing (high p99)

Thanks for flagging this, Ali — sorry for the disruption.

Looping in SRE and runtime engineering. Marissa, Diego: can you triage the attached traces and confirm whether this looks like a KV-cache eviction, kernel contention, or autoscaler chatter?

Immediate asks from our side:
- Short update to Ali in ~30m with what we've observed so far.
- If mitigation is straightforward (fallback to smaller model variant, temporary routing to reserved plane), propose it and I'll coordinate.
- Product ask: if this is caused by the new batching recombinator (rolled out last week), we need a rollback plan and an impact estimate for Checkoutly.

Ali: I'll coordinate comms with you while we triage — please keep the logs coming and let me know if you want a bridge.

— Logan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ali Khatri <ali@checkoutly.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden jitter on /v1/generate - Checkout failing (high p99)

Quick triage notes (30m):
- Observed p99 bump from ~220ms to ~900–1.2s across the us-west cluster starting 07:48 PDT.
- No error spike; success rates unchanged. Traffic patterns show increased short-sequence fanout from Checkoutly (many small prompts at burst QPS).
- KV cache hit-rate for checkoutly decreased ~35% during the window; eviction logs show a correlated GC/compaction job starting at 07:47.

Prelim conclusion: increased fanout + concurrent compaction caused KV cache churn and longer decode times on some workers (cold KV lookups and higher memory pressure). Not seeing immediate kernel-level regressions.

Mitigation options (ordered by speed of rollback):
1) Route Checkoutly to reserved plane that has warmed KV and higher capacity (minutes). I can request a short reservation.
2) Apply a temporary policy to reduce batching window for their route (reduces memory pressure; low risk).
3) Roll back last-week batching recombinator (higher risk; needs product signoff).

Kimberly (product): do we want to authorize (1) or (2) now and then schedule a deeper root-cause RCA? Diego, can you prepare a minimal kernel/trace slice for the RCA?

Attaching a short p99 snapshot.

— Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
[attachment: runtime-sample-logs-15jun.zip]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ali Khatri <ali@checkoutly.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden jitter on /v1/generate - Checkout failing (high p99)

Log slice and technical notes:
- I pulled the worker traces referenced in the zip. The timeline shows frequent small requests that failed to benefit from prefix/KV cache due to TTL bumping and compaction kicking in. One compaction run overlapped with a short burst from Checkoutly causing ~12% of requests to pay cold-costs.
- Root cause appears to be an interaction: our compaction window thresholds (recently tightened to reclaim memory under experimental telemetry) + Checkoutly's sudden short-prompt fanout. The recombinator rollout is unlikely the primary cause; it's amplifying latency when combined with cache churn.

Short-term mitigations I can implement (ETA 25–35m):
- Pin Checkoutly routes to reserved warm pool (Marissa to request).
- Temporarily widen compaction backoff for the us-west pool (I'll push a config change and monitor).
- Add a per-route sticky-KV warming flag so heavy fanout customers don't hit cold lookups during compaction windows (requires product approval; medium risk).

For the postmortem/roadmap: we should add a telemetry sentinel for compaction-overlap-with-high-fanout and prioritize a KV-warming feature (product).

Diego
Senior Runtime Engineer

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ali Khatri <ali@checkoutly.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden jitter on /v1/generate - Checkout failing (high p99)

Ali — short status update and asks: 

What we did (completed):
- Routed Checkoutly to a reserved warmed plane (effective 14:30 UTC / 07:30 PDT).
- Broadened compaction backoff in us-west to avoid overlap with short bursts.
- Enabled a temporary per-route batching reduction for your traffic to smooth memory pressure.

Immediate impact: p99 returned toward baseline within ~6 minutes of the routing change; Checkoutly telemetry shows a ~65% improvement in user-visible checkout latency. We'll continue to watch for 2 hours and report back.

Next steps (product/roadmap asks):
- Product: prioritize an explicit KV-warming feature and a compaction overlap sentinel (Kimberly, can we slot this in the next quarter planning?).
- Engineering: Diego will prepare an RCA with traces and a repro (ETA 48h).
- CS: Neha, please coordinate a short customer-readout tomorrow and offer a credit for measurable revenue impact; I can draft language.

Ali — are you comfortable if we run retros and share the RCA with your ops team by Friday? If you want a 1:1 readout now, we can jump on a call.

Thanks for the rapid report and for the logs — they helped us narrow this quickly.

— Logan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
